##### utmctl version --help
OVERVIEW: Display the version number of the application.

USAGE: utmctl version [--debug] [--hide]

OPTIONS:
  -d, --debug             Show debug logging.
  --hide                  Hide the main UTM window.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

##### exit=0

##### utmctl list --help
OVERVIEW: Enumerate all registered virtual machines.

USAGE: utmctl list [--debug] [--hide]

OPTIONS:
  -d, --debug             Show debug logging.
  --hide                  Hide the main UTM window.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

##### exit=0

##### utmctl status --help
OVERVIEW: Query the status of a virtual machine.

USAGE: utmctl status [--debug] [--hide] <identifier>

ARGUMENTS:
  <identifier>            Either the UUID or the complete name of the virtual
                          machine.

OPTIONS:
  -d, --debug             Show debug logging.
  --hide                  Hide the main UTM window.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

##### exit=0

##### utmctl start --help
OVERVIEW: Start a virtual machine or resume a suspended virtual machine.

USAGE: utmctl start [--debug] [--hide] <identifier> [--attach] [--disposable] [--recovery]

ARGUMENTS:
  <identifier>            Either the UUID or the complete name of the virtual
                          machine.

OPTIONS:
  -d, --debug             Show debug logging.
  --hide                  Hide the main UTM window.
  -a, --attach            Attach to the first serial port after start.
  --disposable            Run VM as a snapshot and do not save changes to disk.
  --recovery              Boot a VM in recovery mode.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

##### exit=0

##### utmctl suspend --help
OVERVIEW: Suspend running a virtual machine to memory.

USAGE: utmctl suspend [--debug] [--hide] <identifier> [--save-state]

ARGUMENTS:
  <identifier>            Either the UUID or the complete name of the virtual
                          machine.

OPTIONS:
  -d, --debug             Show debug logging.
  --hide                  Hide the main UTM window.
  -s, --save-state        Save the VM state to disk after suspending.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

##### exit=0

##### utmctl stop --help
OVERVIEW: Shuts down a running virtual machine.

USAGE: utmctl stop [--debug] [--hide] <identifier> [--force] [--kill] [--request]

ARGUMENTS:
  <identifier>            Either the UUID or the complete name of the virtual
                          machine.

OPTIONS:
  -d, --debug             Show debug logging.
  --hide                  Hide the main UTM window.
  --force                 Force stop by sending a power off event (default)
  --kill                  Force kill the VM process
  --request               Request power down from guest operating system
  -h, --help              Show help information.

##### exit=0

##### utmctl attach --help
OVERVIEW: Redirect the serial input/output to this terminal.

USAGE: utmctl attach [--debug] [--hide] <identifier> [--index <index>]

ARGUMENTS:
  <identifier>            Either the UUID or the complete name of the virtual
                          machine.

OPTIONS:
  -d, --debug             Show debug logging.
  --hide                  Hide the main UTM window.
  --index <index>         Index of the serial device to attach to.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

##### exit=0

##### utmctl file --help
OVERVIEW: Guest agent file operations.

USAGE: utmctl file <subcommand>

OPTIONS:
  -h, --help              Show help information.

SUBCOMMANDS:
  pull                    Fetches a file from the guest and output it to stdout.
  push                    Uploads the contents of stdin to the guest.

  See 'utmctl help file <subcommand>' for detailed help.
##### exit=0

##### utmctl exec --help
OVERVIEW: Execute an application on the guest.

The return value of the command will be returned from this tool.

USAGE: utmctl exec [--debug] [--hide] <identifier> [--input] [--env <env> ...] --cmd <cmd> ...

ARGUMENTS:
  <identifier>            Either the UUID or the complete name of the virtual
                          machine.

OPTIONS:
  -d, --debug             Show debug logging.
  --hide                  Hide the main UTM window.
  --input                 Read in standard input and forward it to the guest.
  --env <env>             Set a single environment variable in the format
                          NAME=VALUE
  --cmd <cmd>             Command line to execute on the guest.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

##### exit=0

##### utmctl ip-address --help
OVERVIEW: List all IP addresses associated with network interfaces on the
guest.

IPv4 addresses (if available) will be listed before any IPv6 address.

USAGE: utmctl ip-address [--debug] [--hide] <identifier>

ARGUMENTS:
  <identifier>            Either the UUID or the complete name of the virtual
                          machine.

OPTIONS:
  -d, --debug             Show debug logging.
  --hide                  Hide the main UTM window.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

##### exit=0

##### utmctl clone --help
OVERVIEW: Clone an existing virtual machine.

USAGE: utmctl clone [--debug] [--hide] <identifier> [--name <name>]

ARGUMENTS:
  <identifier>            Either the UUID or the complete name of the virtual
                          machine.

OPTIONS:
  -d, --debug             Show debug logging.
  --hide                  Hide the main UTM window.
  --name <name>
  -h, --help              Show help information.

##### exit=0

##### utmctl delete --help
OVERVIEW: Delete a virtual machine (there is no confirmation).

USAGE: utmctl delete [--debug] [--hide] <identifier>

ARGUMENTS:
  <identifier>            Either the UUID or the complete name of the virtual
                          machine.

OPTIONS:
  -d, --debug             Show debug logging.
  --hide                  Hide the main UTM window.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

##### exit=0

##### utmctl usb --help
OVERVIEW: USB device handling.

USAGE: utmctl usb <subcommand>

OPTIONS:
  -h, --help              Show help information.

SUBCOMMANDS:
  list                    List connected devices.
  connect                 Connect a USB device to a virtual machine.
  disconnect              Disconnect a USB device from a virtual machine.

  See 'utmctl help usb <subcommand>' for detailed help.
##### exit=0

##### utmctl file pull --help
OVERVIEW: CLI tool for controlling UTM virtual machines.

USAGE: utmctl <subcommand>

OPTIONS:
  -h, --help              Show help information.

SUBCOMMANDS:
  version                 Display the version number of the application.
  list                    Enumerate all registered virtual machines.
  status                  Query the status of a virtual machine.
  start                   Start a virtual machine or resume a suspended virtual
                          machine.
  suspend                 Suspend running a virtual machine to memory.
  stop                    Shuts down a running virtual machine.
  attach                  Redirect the serial input/output to this terminal.
  file                    Guest agent file operations.
  exec                    Execute an application on the guest.
  ip-address              List all IP addresses associated with network
                          interfaces on the guest.
  clone                   Clone an existing virtual machine.
  delete                  Delete a virtual machine (there is no confirmation).
  usb                     USB device handling.

  See 'utmctl help <subcommand>' for detailed help.
